title: Consolidate dual post-merge hook implementations with independent guards
context: An upstream merge left duplicate code in hooks.ts and providers.ts — two separate `installPostMergeHook` implementations, one for provenance detection and one for grounding refresh. The duplicates were fixed in the working tree during conflict resolution but failed to stage due to a bad pathspec in an earlier `git add`, so the committed snapshot retained the duplicates while local checks passed against the working tree. Touches invariant(s): con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file).
decision: Merge the two `installPostMergeHook` implementations into a single function that performs both provenance detection (guarded by HUNCH_MERGE_SYNC) and grounding refresh (guarded by HUNCH_SYNC) as two independently-guarded actions within the same mergeBlock. Guards are separate because HUNCH_MERGE_SYNC is for an action that makes no commit and can't re-trigger itself, while HUNCH_SYNC is shared with post-commit and must prevent recursive git-operation recursion.
consequences: Single source of truth for post-merge hook installation and updates
Both actions are guaranteed to ship together as a cohesive unit
Guard variables remain decoupled so they don't interfere with each other's recursion prevention
Reduced code duplication and maintenance burden going forward
alternatives_rejected: Keep two separate implementations (duplicates would diverge and multiply maintenance burden)
Use a single guard for both actions (HUNCH_SYNC recursion would break the grounding refresh)
Omit grounding refresh entirely (docs would drift from store on merges)
